title: Heel Angle Spikes vs Wind Strength
dataSources: NMEA/SignalK data (`nmea:reading`), bilge pump (`bilge:event`), mooring/anchor watch (`mooring:status`), marine weather (`marineweather:forecast`).
app: Marine electronics — NMEA 2000 / SignalK boat networks, bilge, battery and shore-power sensors, anchor-watch GPS, and marine weather feeds — streamed to Splunk HEC via SignalK and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nmea:reading
| stats avg(abs(heel_deg)) as avg_heel, max(abs(heel_deg)) as max_heel, avg(wind_kts) as avg_wind by sail_plan
| sort - max_heel
description: Compares heel behaviour against wind strength and sail configuration.
value: Heel spikes are useful feedback for comfort, speed, reefing habits, and crew confidence.
implementation: Ingest NMEA readings with heel angle, wind, and sail-plan tags; compare average and peak heel by sail plan.
visualization: Sail-plan table of average wind, average heel, and maximum heel.
grandmaExplanation: It maps how much your boat heels under different wind and sail setups, helping you see when comfort and control start to slip.
